name: Jaisalmer
description: Jaisalmer is a medieval desert city rising from the Thar Desert, anchored by a living sandstone fort that still houses residents, temples, and shops. It suits travelers drawn to Rajput architecture, camel safaris, and the raw silence of sand dunes, though the summer heat (May–June, 45°C+) makes it inhospitable outside the October–March window. The city is compact enough to walk but demands patience — touts and pushy camel-safari operators are a consistent friction point.
bases: Jaisalmer City (inside or near the Fort)
nearest_railhead: Jaisalmer Railway Station (JSM) — on the Jodhpur–Jaisalmer metre-gauge/broad-gauge line, about 3 km from the fort
nearest_airport: Jaisalmer Airport (JSA) — civilian terminal about 5 km from the city; limited flights, mostly from Delhi and Jodhpur

attractions.name: Jaisalmer Fort (Sonar Quila)
attractions.description: A UNESCO-listed living sandstone fort built in 1156 CE, still inhabited by around 3,000 residents. The interior maze of lanes, Jain temples, havelis, and rooftop cafes is genuinely atmospheric, though over-tourism and poor drainage are visibly stressing the structure.
attractions.base: Jaisalmer City (inside or near the Fort)

attractions.name: Patwon Ki Haveli
attractions.description: A cluster of five connected havelis built by a wealthy merchant family in the early 19th century, famous for their extraordinarily detailed sandstone jali screens and carved facades. The ground-floor portions open as a museum; upper floors require a separate ticket and some stair-climbing.
attractions.base: Jaisalmer City (inside or near the Fort)

attractions.name: Salim Singh Ki Haveli
attractions.description: An unusually tall 18th-century haveli with a distinctive blue-arched top floor said to resemble a peacock's neck. It is still partly occupied by descendants of the original owner, which limits access to the exterior and lower floors but adds a layer of authenticity.
attractions.base: Jaisalmer City (inside or near the Fort)

attractions.name: Nathmal Ki Haveli
attractions.description: A 19th-century prime minister's residence notable for its asymmetrical but nearly identical twin facades, each carved by a different master craftsman. Less crowded than Patwon Ki Haveli and often skipped by package tourists, making it an easy walk with fewer touts.
attractions.base: Jaisalmer City (inside or near the Fort)

attractions.name: Sam Sand Dunes
attractions.description: The most accessible and famous dune field, about 42 km west of Jaisalmer, with dunes reaching 30–60 m. Camel rides and overnight camp stays are the draw; the trade-off is heavy commercialization — dozens of noisy camps, blaring music, and crowds at sunset make solitude difficult unless you walk 20 minutes beyond the main staging area.

attractions.name: Khuri Sand Dunes
attractions.description: A quieter dune area about 48 km south-west of Jaisalmer, surrounding the small mud-plastered village of Khuri. The experience is more intimate than Sam — smaller camps, fewer tourists, and village women sometimes performing folk music — though the dunes are shorter and less dramatic.

attractions.name: Gadisar Lake
attractions.description: A 14th-century artificial reservoir just outside the city walls, edged with cenotaphs, temples, and a carved gateway. Morning light on the still water and migratory birds in winter make it a pleasant 45-minute stop; paddleboats are available but the water quality is unremarkable.
attractions.base: Jaisalmer City (inside or near the Fort)

attractions.name: Desert National Park
attractions.description: One of India's largest national parks at 3,162 sq km, protecting cold desert habitat including the critically endangered Great Indian Bustard. Entry requires a permit and a jeep with a guide; wildlife sightings are unpredictable and the terrain is stark, so this rewards patient, wildlife-focused travelers rather than casual visitors.

attractions.name: Bada Bagh (Royal Cenotaphs)
attractions.description: A garden complex about 6 km north of the city containing chhatri cenotaphs of the Bhati rulers, spanning the 16th to 20th century. The golden sandstone glows dramatically at sunset, making this one of the better photography stops; the site is flat and easy to walk, though the surrounding context is mainly scrubland.
attractions.base: Jaisalmer City (inside or near the Fort)

attractions.name: Kuldhara Abandoned Village
attractions.description: A ghost village about 18 km west of Jaisalmer, abandoned overnight in the 1820s by its Paliwal Brahmin inhabitants reportedly to escape an oppressive minister. The ruins of stone houses and a small temple survive in a haunting state of preservation; the site is genuinely evocative and far less visited than the main fort attractions.
attractions.base: Jaisalmer City (inside or near the Fort)
